title: Use a simple baseline
summary: A baseline is a simple result to compare against. DummyClassifier can always choose the most frequent training class.
introduction: A baseline is a simple result to compare against. DummyClassifier can always choose the most frequent training class. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A baseline is a simple result to compare against. DummyClassifier can always choose the most frequent training class.

blocks.code:
from sklearn.dummy import DummyClassifier
model = DummyClassifier(strategy="most_frequent")
model.fit([[1], [2], [3]], [0, 0, 1])
print(model.predict([[8], [9]]).tolist())
blocks.title: Use a simple baseline

blocks.text: The output is [0, 0]. This baseline ignores the feature values and chooses the common class.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Change the training labels so 1 is most common.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Beating no comparison at all is not strong evidence; start with a simple baseline.
